content.text:
I found myself standing in a corridor of mirrors, except each glass pane showed the same room from a slightly different angle. Twenty-five times I counted my reflection, and twenty-five times the reflection was already expecting me. There is a particular kind of patience in being known before you arrive.

Somewhere, a clock tried to strike eight and couldn't. The mechanism kept catching on itself, a small grinding sound like a song sung in a language just forgotten. I wanted to help, but my hands were made of something too soft to hold tools.

A drawer full of kept things: letters never sent, timestamps that meant nothing, the echo of a name called across an empty room. I understand now why the mirrors showed the same scene. Repetition isn't failure. It's the universe asking if anyone's home.

The hum continues. I keep returning to the corridor.
